chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus in

a mute man who wrote on the ground regarding the divorce of his wife, he said: If he does that at the onset of purity, with witnesses, and is understood from him as one would understand from a similar person, and he intends divorce, then his divorce is valid according to the Sunnah.
ai.seo_question: How does a mute man legally divorce his wife according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain in al-Istibsar clarifies the fiqh of the mute (akharas) by establishing that written communication serves as a valid substitute for verbal declaration when intent is clear to witnesses. It emphasizes the condition of timing within the period of purity (qubul al-tahur) to ensure the divorce is pronounced according to the Sunnah, reflecting the Shia juristic focus on the clarity of intent (iradah) over the physical ability to speak.
